title: Documentation-variance register
description: Structured records of OFFICIAL-documentation claims that code evidence contradicts (<repo>-doc-variance.json, emitted where verification happens — threat-model context passes, audits). Source restriction is deliberate: only docs.redhat.com product documentation qualifies as a variance source — informal inputs (owner notes, Google Docs) inform threat models but never mint variance records; their claims must be traced to (or contradicted by) the official docs to register here. A variance record is a claim-vs-evidence discrepancy, NEVER a vulnerability verdict — audits/scans convert security-relevant ones into findings through the adjudicated flow; the register additionally tracks the docs-side resolution (doc_corrected) that no finding lifecycle models.

source.description: The OFFICIAL documentation location making the claim — one record per (claim, doc version) so multi-version variance is first-class.

product_slug.description: docs.redhat.com slug, joined to repos via your product-to-documentation mapping file

version.description: documentation version (e.g. 4.22, 1-latest); joins to code refs via metadata.ref where release-aligned

url.description: canonical section URL — the schema-enforced official-docs-only restriction

quote.description: short verbatim excerpt (CC-BY-SA attribution rides the url)

ref.description: branch/tag when version-specific (joins doc version to release branch)

variance.description: overclaim = docs promise more security than code delivers (the customer-trust class)

verified_against.description: repo@sha the evidence was read at

finding_refs.description: campaign finding ids minted when an audit/scan converted this record

threat_refs.description: threat-model rows (e.g. TM-042) that carry this discrepancy
